summary: JSON Pointer is a Standards Track document from the Internet Engineering Task Force that defines a string syntax for identifying a specific value within a JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) document. A pointer is evaluated from the root of the document, and it can be written either as a JSON string or as a Uniform Resource Identifier fragment. It does not define what happens when a pointer fails, because the RFC leaves error handling to each application that uses it. A trap for a standards audience: a document being JSON does not mean pointers work as its fragment, since the fragment syntax for the application/json media type is not JSON Pointer, and each media type has to adopt it explicitly.

sources.title: RFC 6901, Status of This Memo
sources.quote: This is an Internet Standards Track document.

sources.title: RFC 6901, Section 4 Evaluation
sources.quote: Evaluation of a JSON Pointer begins with a reference to the root value of a JSON document and completes with a reference to some value within the document.

sources.title: RFC 6901, Section 4 Evaluation
sources.quote: Thus, applications of JSON Pointer need to specify how that character is to be handled, if it is to be useful.

sources.title: RFC 6901, Section 6 URI Fragment Identifier Representation
sources.quote: In particular, the fragment identifier syntax for application/json is not JSON Pointer.

sources.title: RFC 6901, Section 5 JSON String Representation
sources.quote: A JSON Pointer can be represented in a JSON string value.

sources.title: RFC 6901, Section 6 URI Fragment Identifier Representation
sources.quote: A JSON Pointer can be represented in a URI fragment identifier by encoding it into octets using UTF-8 [RFC3629], while percent-encoding those characters not allowed by the fragment rule in [RFC3986].
